legend: FNAB of cervical lymph node, direct smears. Left: Whole slide: The entire sample, consisting mainly of clotted blood, was used to make one smear. Right: Low power: Abundant lymphoid tissue is present, caught up in and obscured by fibrin clot cast of the fine needle, a result of delayed transfer from the needle to the slide (H&E).

diagnosis: Paucicellular lymphoid smear with air-drying artefact
legend: FNAB of cervical lymph node. All of the cells obtained by this FNAB are present in one high-power field. Many of the cells on the right side of the image show air-drying artefact and cannot be assessed. The specimen was reported as insufficient due to low cellularity and air-drying artefact. The presence of a mast cell is noted (Pap).
FNAB of lymph node. Low power showing deeply stained featureless material, consistent with ultrasound gel, obscuring the cells that are present (Giemsa).

FNAB of lymph node showing gross contamination with ultrasound gel, which completely obscures cellular detail. Because atypical cells were identified, this specimen was reported as “Suspicious” rather than “Inadequate”, noting the technical limitations (Giemsa).

FNAB of axillary lymph node. The entire sample is reflected in a single fragment of adipose tissue infiltrated by small lymphocytes, insufficient to resolve the clinical differential diagnosis of lipomatous lymph node versus indolent lymphoma (liquid-based cytopathology, Pap).

FNAB of axillary lymph node. At higher power, the single fragment of adipose tissue can be seen to be infiltrated by small lymphocytes, insufficient to resolve the clinical differential diagnosis of lipomatous lymph node versus indolent lymphoma (Pap).
